drafts.subject: Re: Guest lecture on agentic programming?
drafts.message:
Dear Professor Alvarez,

Thank you for reaching out and for your interest in Jaseci. We are delighted to hear that your students have been experimenting with the framework, and we would be glad to contribute a guest lecture to your graduate seminar on AI systems.

We can confirm that a member of the Jaseci team will be available to present a 60-minute session on agentic programming. Of the two dates you proposed, September 22 works best on our end. We will plan to present during the 2–4pm Eastern window, and we are happy to present remotely via Zoom (or your preferred platform).

To make the session as useful as possible for your students, it would be helpful to know a little more about their prior experience with Jaseci and the Jac language, as well as any specific topics you would like us to emphasize (for example, walkers and graph traversal, building agentic workflows, or deploying agents at scale). If you could share a brief syllabus or list of topics already covered, we can tailor the lecture accordingly. We will also prepare a short set of example code and slides in advance and are happy to share those with you beforehand for feedback.

Please let us know the preferred remote platform and any access or scheduling details, and we will follow up with a confirmed agenda and materials.

We look forward to speaking with your seminar.

Best regards,
The Jaseci Team
impact@jaseci.org

drafts.subject: Re: Quick question | byLLM structured output
drafts.message:
Hi Priya,

Good news — byLLM supports structured/typed outputs natively, so you won't need to manually parse the model's text output.

byLLM is our LLM integration framework for the Jac language. You can declare a function with a typed return value (including structured objects) and delegate the implementation to the LLM using the `by llm()` syntax. The runtime enforces that the model's output conforms to the declared type, so you get back structured data directly.

For your log triage use case, you'd define a return type that matches your fields and let byLLM handle the rest. A sketch of how this looks in Jac:

```
struct LogEntry {
    severity: str;
    component: str;
    message: str;
}

fn triage_log(log_line: str) -> LogEntry by llm();
```

When you call `triage_log("ERROR | walker_spawn | context missing")`, byLLM returns a `LogEntry` with `severity`, `component`, and `message` populated — no regex or manual parsing required on your end.

A few practical notes:

- The model is prompted to produce output matching the declared type; the runtime validates/constrains the response accordingly.
- You can use this with a list return type (e.g., `list[LogEntry]`) if you're batching multiple log lines in a single call.
- This works with any backend LLM byLLM supports; the structured output enforcement is handled at the framework level.

Happy to share a more complete example or hop on a quick call to walk through the setup. Let me know what's most useful.

Best,
Jaseci Team
impact@jaseci.org
